title: Israel builds 90km network of military roads across southern Lebanon
summary: Israel is building roads and military outposts across southern Lebanon.

title: Iran’s IRGC says building underground sites for weapons production, storage
summary: IRGC says underground military complexes allow missile production to continue even under heavy bombardment.

title: Buildings damaged in Israeli bombings risk collapse as rain inundates Gaza
summary: Floods have swept through Gaza after heavy rain, endangering families and putting war-damaged buildings at risk.

title: Pro-Russian hackers leak Italian foreign minister’s data on dark web
summary: The prime minister blames pro-Russian hackers for the leak, as her top diplomat says the cyberthreat was ongoing.

title: Dozens killed as humanitarian crisis mounts in Yemen: What next for war?
summary: Government forces reclaim key territories in Taiz and Lahij but face setbacks under Houthi resistance in certain areas.

title: Paraguay's president impeached and under house arrest after bank collapse
summary: Santiago Peña was ousted due to a banking crisis which left millions of people unable to access their money.

title: Spate of bomb threats poses serious challenge to airline industry
summary: After a week of disruption, airlines are facing both safety and financial concerns.

title: New wave of bomb threats hit European airlines
summary: No link has been established between the threats against the airlines and those against the media outlets.

title: Afghanistan faces deepening humanitarian crisis amid sweeping rights restrictions
summary: Afghanistan stands at a “difficult crossroad” more than five years after the Taliban returned to power, a senior UN official said on Friday. Relative stability and security are being undercut by a fragile economy, sweeping curbs on rights and acute humanitarian need.

title: From a ship frozen into Arctic ice, a warning to world leaders: Trust the science
summary: Drifting through the polar darkness, a team of scientists is documenting a rapidly changing Arctic. As sea ice retreats and oil tankers move in, a conversation with the UN chief reveals why the battle for climate science matters far beyond the North Pole.

title: Sudan’s suffering is plain for all to see say aid teams, as brutal war continues
summary: Aid teams working to help millions of people uprooted by the ongoing war in Sudan appealed on Friday for more international assistance amid desperate funding shortages, empty warehouses and overwhelming needs.

title: ‘No Escape’ for refugees on the frontlines of the climate crisis
summary: The climate emergency is an immediate crisis for refugees, with three in four – nearly 90 million people – living in countries facing high to severe exposure to hazards such as drought, floods and extreme heat.

title: Bomb hoaxes: Messages reveal how threat was passed on by air traffic control
summary: BBC Verify has been analysing messages after flights across Europe were targeted by fake bomb threats - the second such incident this week.

title: World News in Brief: Korea tensions mount, UN demands answers over staff death in Yemen, Guterres in Spain, Nepal alert ahead of COP31
summary: UN Secretary-General António Guterres remains concerned over the situation on the Korean Peninsula, including the potential escalation of tensions across the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ), his Spokesperson said on Thursday.

title: Abyei: Deadly drone strikes mark ‘new and concerning’ threat, UN peacekeeping chief warns
summary: Drone strikes that killed at least 30 people in Abyei last month have added “a new and concerning dimension” to security in the disputed area, the UN’s peacekeeping chief told the Security Council on Thursday.

title: Children at risk as war zone attacks on water and sanitation more than triple
summary: Attacks that damaged or destroyed water and sanitation systems in conflict zones tripled between 2021 and 2025, increasing children’s risk of exposure to disease outbreaks, malnutrition and violence.

title: UN peacekeeping chief warns of ‘security vacuum’ as Blue Helmets leave Lebanon and Western Sahara
summary: The UN’s peacekeeping chief warned on Wednesday that the withdrawal of “Blue Helmets” from Lebanon and Western Sahara risks leaving a dangerous security vacuum, while the Security Council remains divided over what, if anything, should replace them.

title: Gunfire damages tents at Rafah displacement site in Gaza, as aid teams prepare for winter storms
summary: Gunfire hit and damaged multiple tents at a displacement site in Gaza’s northern Rafah region on Tuesday, reportedly causing injuries and forcing a humanitarian partner to leave the area, the UN aid coordination office (OCHA) has said.

title: Fuel price shock: Why developing economies are paying the most at the pump
summary: When war shut the Strait of Hormuz in February, oil prices soared everywhere. But the pain at the pump has been far from equal, and the world’s developing economies are paying the heaviest price, according to a new report from UNCTAD, the UN trade and development agency.

title: Syria’s undocumented children ‘pay the price’ of war and a law that shuts out mothers
summary: Many children born in Syria since the war began in 2011 have no legal identity because nationality passes only through fathers – many of whom are dead or missing – a member of the independent UN commission investigating rights violations in the country said on Wednesday.

title: ‘The world is not ready’: Climate adaptation cash falls far short as warming heads past 1.5°C
summary: Although global warming is set to exceed 1.5°C, financing to help communities adapt to climate change falls far short of needs, the UN Environment Programme (UNEP) said in a report published on Wednesday.

title: ‘This is not about politics. This is about people’: UN warns of impact of deadly drone strikes in Sudan
summary: Intensifying drone attacks on civilian infrastructure across Sudan are disrupting electricity, water and fuel supplies, putting lives at risk and hampering the delivery of humanitarian aid, the UN’s top official in the country has warned.

title: Married off at 14: In Yemen’s war, women and girls suffer ‘devastating consequences’
summary: Safa is 14. Her mother died earlier this year. She has no brothers or sisters. And a few weeks ago, as the crisis took hold, her father married her to an elderly man, afraid that if he were killed in the hostilities, no one would be left to protect her.

title: Air raid alerts and attacks on schools: the devastating face of education in Ukraine
summary: Ukraine has sustained almost 2,000 attacks on education since the full-scale Russian invasion in 2022, with some 270 this year alone, the UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF) said on Tuesday, a day after a strike at a school being used to distribute aid.

title: World News in Brief: healthcare crisis in Yemen’s Taiz and Afghanistan, Western Sahara mission's phased closure
summary: The humanitarian crisis in Yemen is worsening, particularly in the southwestern city of Taiz, which is being encircled by paramilitary Iran-backed Houthi forces.

title: Ukraine: WFP provides hot meals to Oleshky evacuees as UN pushes to restore power before winter
summary: The UN World Food Programme (WFP) is providing emergency food assistance to more than 400 people who were able to leave the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky, in Ukraine’s Kherson region, during a brief local ceasefire.

title: Ethiopia: Violence in the north is pushing health system to the brink, WHO chief warns
summary: The head of the World Health Organization (WHO) called on Monday for greater protection for civilians caught in conflict in northern Ethiopia following deadly drone strikes this past weekend.

title: Six in seven journalist murders go unpunished,  UNESCO reports
summary: Global impunity for journalist killings has risen for the first time in more than a decade, while the growing use of drones is an emerging threat for reporters in conflict zones, according to the latest report from UN cultural organization UNESCO.
